Congress just voted down the Venezuela War Powers Resolution, 211–213.

A War Powers Resolution is Congress using its constitutional authority to say: the president does not have approval to engage US military forces in a conflict without explicit authorization. It is not a declaration of war. It is a leash. When passed, it limits or ends unauthorized military involvement, usually airstrikes, special operations, advisors, or “temporary” deployments that quietly turn into forever wars. 🧵⏬

content: It makes no sense how the Bel-Air series finale had me sobbing. It was so perfect! It is one of the few Black shows from beginning to end that showed how Black excellence can coexist with being flawed, layered, and complicated. I'm going to miss having a show rooted in a Black family that loves each other, works through conflict in a healthy way, and supports one another.  Bravo to the cast and crew on a brilliant four seasons!

I’ve been thinking a lot about selective outrage lately.

If moral urgency only activates for one conflict, one narrative, one kind of protest, it isn’t moral clarity, it’s just performative. 

Justice was never meant to be convenient or singular. It’s meant to be expansive...something we are meant to continually pursue. And if our sense of responsibility can’t stretch to hold more than one truth at a time, then it isn’t justice.

So let’s talk about what that looks like in real time. 🧵
